neighbours.label: ' it' or comma inside short fixed exclamations and catchphrases (that's it, stop it, go on,)
fire: When the last guest finally left, Mom sighed and said, well, that's it for tonight.
The kids kept poking each other until their father snapped, stop it, both of you.
Her old poster read Love It, Leave It in big red letters across the top.
He grinned at the frightened crowd and shouted, it's alive, it's alive!
The coach clapped twice and yelled, go on, get back out there and run.
After three hours of arguing the manager just shrugged and said, forget it.
She waved the puppy toward the door and whispered, go, get your ball.
My grandfather always ended his stories the same way: and that was it, kids.
quiet: When the last guest finally left, Mom sighed and started washing the dishes.
The kids kept poking each other until their father moved them to separate rooms.
Her old poster showed a map of Europe in faded red and blue ink.
He looked at the frightened crowd and slowly lowered the heavy lantern.
The coach clapped twice and the players jogged back onto the field.
After three hours of arguing the manager agreed to postpone the decision.
She opened the door and the puppy ran outside to find its ball.
My grandfather always ended his stories with a long sip of black coffee.
